_why: CCR records one model under several spellings in usage_events.model (with a provider prefix, with a build date, with an expiry note). Aggregating cost by the raw string splits one model across several rows and under-reports it. The generic rules (strip provider prefix, strip -expires-on-<date>, strip a trailing 4-digit build date, strip a [1m] marker) handle most cases; this file is only for aliases the generic rules cannot infer.
_maintain: To add an alias, edit this file only — no code change needed. The left-hand key is the NORMALIZED name (provider prefix and date suffixes already stripped). The right-hand value is the logical model name you want everything merged into.

_not_aliased_example.<model>-vision-exp: A vision-capable variant is a distinct capability — do NOT merge it into the text-only model.
_not_aliased_example.<model>-v4.1: v4.1 and v4 are different versions; the generic rules already keep them apart.

_free_why: CCR's cost_usd is ESTIMATED from a pricing table (cost_source = models.dev / litellm), not read from a bill. A free provider still gets a positive estimate: measured — one free provider was costed at $10.45 by the litellm table, while another showed $0 only because it had no pricing entry at all. If you do not declare free providers here, the report treats free quota as real spend.
_free_maintain: Match by PREFIX. Runtime provider names may carry a suffix, e.g. `myprovider::openai_chat_completions::cred:key-1-1` — listing `myprovider` covers all of them.
